item.title: Devin Royal Settling in Offensively at Small Forward Position, Working on Ball Security
item.description: Devin Royal’s performance against Minnesota is analogous to his 2025-26 season – it required an adjustment. item.title: Davison Igbinosun, CJ Donaldson, Ethan Onianwa Among Buckeyes Looking to Boost Their NFL Draft Stock in All-Star Games
item.description: Several members of the 2025 Ohio State football team will play one more football game in an Ohio State helmet over the next 10 days as they look to bolster their NFL draft stock by performing well in pre-draft all-star games. Former Ohio State offensive lineman Ethan Onianwa and long snapper John Ferlmann will be among the participants in The American Bowl, a new pre-draft all-star game that will be played Thursday night (8 p.m., NFL Network) in Lakeland, Florida. item.title: Ohio State Women’s Basketball Overcomes Slow Start to Defeat Indiana, 81-67, for Seventh Straight Win
item.description: Ohio State women’s basketball battled back in the second half to avoid an upset loss vs. Indiana. The Buckeyes never led in the first half and trailed by as many as 12 points in the third quarter against the Hoosiers, but took control of the game in the final 18 minutes to earn an 81-67 win and avoid suffering their first loss of the season to an unranked opponent. item.title: Ohio State to Replace Scoreboard in Schottenstein Center
item.description: The Schottenstein Center will have a new look above center court (and across the arena) beginning next season. For the first time since 2008, Ohio State is set to replace the scoreboard in the arena, a project that was approved by the Board of Trustees and will begin in April. Eighteen years ago, the replacement and upgrade celebrated the 10th season of basketball played at the Schottenstein Center. Nearly two decades later, it's time to give the arena an updated look. item.title: No. 3 Michigan Takes Control With 21-6 Second-Half Run, Defeats Ohio State in Ann Arbor, 74-62
item.description: Ohio State ran out of gas with eight minutes still on the clock in Ann Arbor, Michigan. The No. 3 Wolverines (18-1, 8-1 Big Ten) led the Buckeyes (13-6, 5-4) just 52-51 at that point of the game, but quickly launched a 21-6 run to generate the separation many expected when Ohio State entered the hostile confines of the Crisler Center on Friday.
